paragraph.content: Of the funds authorized to be appropriated under subsection (k) of section 306 of the Department of Energy Research and Innovation Act (42 U.S.C. 18644) for a fiscal year, there is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this subsection $30,000,000 per center established under paragraph (1) for each of fiscal years 2023 through 2027.

paragraph.heading: Definitions.—
paragraph.chapeau: In this subsection:

subparagraph.heading: Advanced biofuel.—
subparagraph.content: The term “advanced biofuel” has the meaning given the term in section 9001 of the Farm Security and Rural Investment Act of 2002 (7 U.S.C. 8101).

subparagraph.heading: Bioenergy.—
subparagraph.content: The term “bioenergy” means energy derived from biofuels.

subparagraph.heading: Biomass.—
subparagraph.content: The term “biomass” has the meaning given the term in section 203(b) of the Energy Policy Act of 2005 (42 U.S.C. 15852(b)).

subparagraph.heading: Bioproduct.—
subparagraph.content: The term “bioproduct” has the meaning given the term “biobased product” in section 9001 of the Farm Security and Rural Investment Act of 2002 (7 U.S.C. 8101).

section.heading: FISSION AND FUSION ENERGY MATERIALS RESEARCH PROGRAM.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: Along with the budget request of the President submitted to Congress for fiscal year 2007, the Secretary shall establish a research and development program on material science issues presented by advanced fission reactors and the fusion energy program of the Department.

subsection.heading: Administration.—
subsection.chapeau: In carrying out the program, the Secretary shall develop—

paragraph.content: a catalog of material properties required for applications described in subsection (a);
theoretical models for materials possessing the required properties;
benchmark models against existing data; and
a roadmap to guide further research and development in the area covered by the program.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall carry out a program of research, development, demonstration, and commercial application to—

paragraph.content: address energy-related issues associated with provision of adequate water supplies, optimal management, and efficient use of water;
address water-related issues associated with the provision of adequate supplies, optimal management, and efficient use of energy; and
assess the effectiveness of existing programs within the Department and other Federal agencies to address these energy and water related issues.

subsection.heading: Program Elements.—
subsection.chapeau: The program under this section shall include—

paragraph.content: arsenic treatment;
desalination; and
planning, analysis, and modeling of energy and water supply and demand.

subsection.heading: Collaboration.—
subsection.content: In carrying out this section, the Secretary shall consult with the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, the Secretary of the Interior, the Chief Engineer of the Army Corps of Engineers, the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of Defense, and other Federal agencies as appropriate.

subsection.heading: Facilities.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may utilize all existing facilities within the Department and may design and construct additional facilities as needed to carry out the purposes of this program.

subsection.heading: Advisory Committee.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall establish or utilize an advisory committee to provide independent advice and review of the program.

subsection.heading: Reports.—
subsection.content: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report on the assessment described in subsection (b) and recommendations for future actions.

subsection.heading: Definitions.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section:

paragraph.heading: SING.—
paragraph.content: The term “SING” means the Spallation Neutron Source Instruments Next Generation major item of equipment.

paragraph.heading: SNS power upgrade.—
paragraph.content: The term “SNS power upgrade” means the Spallation Neutron Source power upgrade described in the 20-year facilities plan of the Office of Science of the Department.

paragraph.heading: SNS second target station.—
paragraph.content: The term “SNS second target station” means the Spallation Neutron Source second target station described in the 20-year facilities plan of the Office of Science of the Department.

paragraph.heading: Spallation neutron source facility.—
paragraph.content: The terms “Spallation Neutron Source Facility” and “Facility” mean the completed Spallation Neutron Source scientific user facility located at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak Ridge, Tennessee.

paragraph.heading: Spallation neutron source project.—
paragraph.content: The terms “Spallation Neutron Source Project” and “Project” means Department Project 99–E–334, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak Ridge, Tennessee.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall submit to Congress, as part of the annual budget request of the President submitted to Congress, a report on progress on the Spallation Neutron Source Project.

paragraph.heading: Contents.—
paragraph.chapeau: The report shall include for the Project—

subparagraph.content: a description of the achievement of milestones;
a comparison of actual costs to estimated costs; and
any changes in estimated Project costs or schedule.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall develop an operational plan for the Spallation Neutron Source Facility that ensures that the Facility is employed to the full capability of the Facility in support of the study of advanced materials, nanoscience, and other missions of the Office of Science of the Department.

paragraph.heading: Plan.—
paragraph.chapeau: The operational plan shall—

subparagraph.chapeau: include a plan for the operation of an effective scientific user program that—

clause.content: is based on peer review of proposals submitted for use of the Facility;

includes scientific and technical support to ensure that external users, including researchers based at institutions of higher education, are able to make full use of a variety of high quality scientific instruments; and
phases in systems upgrades to ensure that the Facility remains at the forefront of international scientific endeavors in the field of the Facility throughout the operating life of the Facility;

subparagraph.content: include an ongoing program to develop new instruments that builds on the high performance neutron source and that allows neutron scattering techniques to be applied to a growing range of scientific problems and disciplines; and

subparagraph.chapeau: address the status of and, to the maximum extent practicable, costs and schedules for—

clause.content: full user mode operations of the Facility;
instrumentation built at the Facility during the operating phase through full use of the experimental hall, including the SING;
the SNS power upgrade; and
the SNS second target station.

paragraph.heading: Spallation neutron source project.—
paragraph.chapeau: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out the Spallation Neutron Source Project for the lifetime of the Project $1,411,700,000 for total project costs, of which—

subparagraph.content: $1,192,700,000 shall be used for the costs of construction; and
$219,000,000 shall be used for other Project costs.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Except as provided in subparagraph (B), there is authorized to be appropriated for the Spallation Neutron Source Facility for—

clause.content: the SING, $75,000,000 for each of fiscal year 2007 through 2009; and
the SNS power upgrade, $160,000,000, to remain available until expended.

subparagraph.heading: Insufficient stockpiles of heavy water.—
subparagraph.content: If stockpiles of heavy water of the Department are insufficient to meet the needs of the Facility, there is authorized to be appropriated for the Facility $12,000,000 for fiscal year 2007.

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall construct and operate a Facility for Rare Isotope Beams. The Secretary shall commence construction no later than September 30, 2008.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary such sums as may be necessary to carry out this section. The Secretary shall not spend more than $1,100,000,000 in Federal funds for all activities associated with the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams, prior to operation of the Accelerator.

section.heading: OFFICE OF SCIENTIFIC AND TECHNICAL INFORMATION.
section.content: The Secretary, through the Office of Scientific and Technical Information, shall maintain within the Department publicly available collections of scientific and technical information resulting from research, development, demonstration, and commercial applications activities supported by the Department.

section.heading: SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING EDUCATION PILOT PROGRAM.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Pilot Program.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall award a grant to a Southeastern United States consortium of major research universities that currently advances science and education by partnering with National Laboratories, to establish a regional pilot program of its SEEK–16 program for enhancing scientific, technological, engineering, and mathematical literacy, creativity, and decision-making. The consortium shall include leading research universities, one or more universities that train substantial numbers of elementary and secondary school teachers, and (where appropriate) National Laboratories.

subsection.heading: Program Elements.—
subsection.chapeau: The regional pilot program shall include—

paragraph.content: expanding strategic, formal partnerships among universities with strength in research, universities that train substantial numbers of elementary and secondary school teachers, and the private sector;
combining Department expertise with one or more National Aeronautics and Space Administration Educator Resource Centers;
developing programs to permit current and future teachers to participate in ongoing research projects at National Laboratories and research universities and to adapt lessons learned to the classroom;
designing and implementing course work;
designing and implementing a strategy for measuring and assessing progress under the program; and
developing models for transferring knowledge gained under the pilot program to other institutions and areas of the United States.

subsection.heading: Categorization.—
subsection.content: A grant under this section shall be considered an authorized activity under section 3165 of the Department of Energy Science Education Enhancement Act (42 U.S.C. 7381b).

subsection.heading: Postdoctoral Fellowship Program.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall establish a program under which the Secretary provides fellowships to encourage outstanding young scientists and engineers to pursue postdoctoral research appointments in energy research and development at institutions of higher education of their choice.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall establish a program under which the Secretary provides fellowships to allow outstanding senior researchers and their research groups in energy research and development to explore research and development topics of their choosing for a period of not less than 3 years, to be determined by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Consideration.—
paragraph.chapeau: In providing a fellowship under the program described in paragraph (1), the Secretary shall consider—

subparagraph.content: the past scientific or technical accomplishment of a senior researcher; and
the potential for continued accomplishment by the researcher during the period of the fellowship.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary is authorized to establish a Science and Technology Scholarship Program to award scholarships to individuals that is designed to recruit and prepare students for careers in the Department and National Laboratories.

subsection.heading: Service Requirement.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may require that an individual receiving a scholarship under this section serve as a full-time employee of the Department or a National Laboratory for a fixed period in return for receiving the scholarship.

subsection.heading: Program.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall carry out a program to promote cooperation on energy issues with countries of the Western Hemisphere.

subsection.heading: Activities.—
subsection.chapeau: Under the program, the Secretary shall fund activities to work with countries of the Western Hemisphere to—

paragraph.content: increase the production of energy supplies;
improve energy efficiency; and
assist in the development and transfer of energy supply and efficiency technologies that would have a beneficial impact on world energy markets.

subsection.heading: Participation by Institutions of Higher Education.—
subsection.chapeau: To the extent practicable, the Secretary shall carry out the program under this section with the participation of institutions of higher education so as to take advantage of the acceptance of institutions of higher education by countries of the Western Hemisphere as sources of unbiased technical and policy expertise when assisting the Secretary in—

paragraph.content: evaluating new technologies;
resolving technical issues;
working with those countries in the development of new policies; and

paragraph.chapeau: training policymakers, particularly in the case of institutions of higher education that involve the participation of minority students, such as—

subparagraph.content: Hispanic-serving institutions; and
part B institutions.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.chapeau: There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section—

paragraph.content: $10,000,000 for fiscal year 2007;
$13,000,000 for fiscal year 2008; and
$16,000,000 for fiscal year 2009.

section.heading: COOPERATION BETWEEN UNITED STATES AND ISRAEL.

subsection.heading: Findings.—
subsection.chapeau: Congress finds that—

paragraph.content: on February 1, 1996, the United States and Israel signed the agreement entitled “Agreement between the Department of Energy of the United States of America and the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure of Israel Concerning Energy Cooperation” (referred to in this section as the “Agreement”), to establish a framework for collaboration between the United States and Israel in energy research and development activities;
the Agreement entered into force in February 2000;
in February 2005, the Agreement was automatically renewed for 1 additional 5-year period pursuant to Article X of the Agreement; and
under the Agreement, the United States and Israel may cooperate in energy research and development in a variety of alternative and advanced energy sectors.

subsection.heading: Report to Congress.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources and the Committee on Foreign Relations of the Senate and the Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Committee on International Relations of the House of Representatives a report that describes—

paragraph.content: the ways in which the United States and Israel have cooperated on energy research and development activities under the Agreement;
projects initiated pursuant to the Agreement; and
plans for future cooperation and joint projects under the Agreement.

subsection.heading: Sense of Congress.—
subsection.content: It is the sense of Congress that energy cooperation between the Governments of the United States and Israel is mutually beneficial in the development of energy technology.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of the Interior, and Secretary of State, and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, shall coordinate training and outreach efforts for international commercial energy markets in countries with developing and restructuring economies.

subsection.heading: Components.—
subsection.chapeau: The training and outreach efforts referred to in subsection (a) may include—

paragraph.content: production-related fiscal regimes;
grid and network issues;
energy user and demand side response;
international trade of energy; and
international transportation of energy.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $1,500,000 for each of fiscal years 2007 through 2010.

section.heading: AVAILABILITY OF FUNDS.
section.content: Funds authorized to be appropriated to the Department under this Act or an amendment made by this Act shall remain available until expended.

subsection.heading: Applicability.—
subsection.content: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, in carrying out a research, development, demonstration, or commercial application program or activity that is initiated after the date of enactment of this section, the Secretary shall require cost-sharing in accordance with this section.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Except as provided in paragraphs (2), (3), and (4) and subsection (f), the Secretary shall require not less than 20 percent of the cost of a research or development activity described in subsection (a) to be provided by a non-Federal source.

paragraph.heading: Exclusion.—
paragraph.content: Paragraph (1) shall not apply to a research or development activity described in subsection (a) that is of a basic or fundamental nature, as determined by the appropriate officer of the Department.

paragraph.heading: Reduction.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may reduce or eliminate the requirement of paragraph (1) for a research and development activity of an applied nature if the Secretary determines that the reduction is necessary and appropriate.

paragraph.heading: Exemption for institutions of higher education and other nonprofit institutions.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Paragraph (1) shall not apply to a research or development activity performed by an institution of higher education or nonprofit institution (as defined in section 4 of the Stevenson-Wydler Technology Innovation Act of 1980 (15 U.S.C. 3703)).

subparagraph.heading: Termination date.—
subparagraph.content: The exemption under subparagraph (A) shall apply during the 2-year period beginning on the date of enactment of the Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Except as provided in paragraph (2) and subsection (f), the Secretary shall require that not less than 50 percent of the cost of a demonstration or commercial application activity described in subsection (a) to be provided by a non-Federal source.

paragraph.heading: Reduction of non-federal share.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may reduce the non-Federal share required under paragraph (1) if the Secretary determines the reduction to be necessary and appropriate, taking into consideration any technological risk relating to the activity.

subsection.heading: Calculation of Amount.—
subsection.chapeau: In calculating the amount of a non-Federal contribution under this section, the Secretary—

paragraph.chapeau: may include allowable costs in accordance with the applicable cost principles, including—

subparagraph.content: cash;
personnel costs;
the value of a service, other resource, or third party in-kind contribution determined in accordance with the applicable circular of the Office of Management and Budget;
indirect costs or facilities and administrative costs; or
any funds received under the power program of the Tennessee Valley Authority (except to the extent that such funds are made available under an annual appropriation Act); and

paragraph.chapeau: shall not include—

subparagraph.content: revenues or royalties from the prospective operation of an activity beyond the time considered in the award;
proceeds from the prospective sale of an asset of an activity; or
other appropriated Federal funds.

subsection.heading: Repayment of Federal Share.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall not require repayment of the Federal share of a cost-shared activity under this section as a condition of making an award.

subsection.heading: Exclusions.—
subsection.chapeau: This section shall not apply to—

paragraph.content: a cooperative research and development agreement under the Stevenson-Wydler Technology Innovation Act of 1980 (15 U.S.C. 3701 et seq.);
a fee charged for the use of a Department facility; or

paragraph.chapeau: an award under—

subparagraph.content: the small business innovation research program under section 9 of the Small Business Act (15 U.S.C. 638); or
the small business technology transfer program under that section.

subsection.heading: Awards.—
subsection.content: Awards of funds authorized under this Act or an amendment made by this Act shall be made only after an impartial review of the scientific and technical merit of the proposals for the awards has been carried out by or for the Department.

subsection.heading: Competition.—
subsection.chapeau: Competitive awards under this Act shall involve competitions open to all qualified entities within one or more of the following categories:

paragraph.content: Institutions of higher education.
National Laboratories.
Nonprofit and for-profit private entities.
State and local governments.
Consortia of entities described in paragraphs (1) through (4).

subsection.heading: Sense of Congress.—
subsection.content: It is the sense of Congress that research, development, demonstration, and commercial application activities carried out by the Department should be awarded using competitive procedures, to the maximum extent practicable.

section.heading: EXTERNAL TECHNICAL REVIEW OF DEPARTMENTAL PROGRAMS.

subsection.heading: National Energy Research and Development Advisory Boards.—

paragraph.heading: Establishment.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall establish one or more advisory boards to review research, development, demonstration, and commercial application programs of the Department in energy efficiency, renewable energy, nuclear energy, and fossil energy.

paragraph.heading: Alternatives.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary may—

subparagraph.content: designate an existing advisory board within the Department to fulfill the responsibilities of an advisory board under this section; and
enter into appropriate arrangements with the National Academy of Sciences to establish such an advisory board.

subsection.heading: Use of Existing Committees.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall continue to use the scientific program advisory committees chartered under chapter 10 of title 5, United States Code, by the Office of Science to oversee research and development programs under that Office.

subsection.heading: Membership.—
subsection.content: Each advisory board under this section shall consist of persons with appropriate expertise representing a diverse range of interests.

paragraph.heading: Meetings.—
paragraph.content: Each advisory board under this section shall meet at least semiannually to review and advise on the progress made by the respective one or more research, development, demonstration, and commercial application programs.

paragraph.heading: Goals.—
paragraph.content: The advisory board shall review the measurable cost and performance-based goals for the programs as established under section 902, and the progress on meeting the goals.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall enter into appropriate arrangements with the National Academy of Sciences to conduct periodic reviews and assessments of—

subparagraph.content: the research, development, demonstration, and commercial application programs authorized by this Act and amendments made by this Act;
the measurable cost and performance-based goals for the programs as established under section 902, if any; and
the progress on meeting the goals.

paragraph.heading: Timing.—
paragraph.content: The reviews and assessments shall be conducted every 5 years or more often as the Secretary considers necessary.

paragraph.heading: Reports.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall submit to Congress reports describing the results of all the reviews and assessments.

section.heading: NATIONAL LABORATORY DESIGNATION.
section.content: After the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall not designate a facility that is not listed in section 2(3) as a National Laboratory.

section.heading: REPORT ON EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY PRACTICES.

subsection.chapeau: Not later than 12 months after the date of enactment of this Act, and biennially thereafter, the Secretary shall transmit to Congress a report on the equal employment opportunity practices at National Laboratories. Such report shall include—

paragraph.content: a thorough review of each National Laboratory contractor's equal employment opportunity policies, including promotion to management and professional positions and pay raises;
a statistical report on complaints and their disposition in the National Laboratories;
a description of how equal employment opportunity practices at the National Laboratories are treated in the contract and in calculating award fees for each contractor;
a summary of disciplinary actions and their disposition by either the Department or the relevant contractors for each National Laboratory;
a summary of outreach efforts to attract women and minorities to the National Laboratories;
a summary of efforts to retain women and minorities in the National Laboratories; and
a summary of collaboration efforts with the Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs to improve equal employment opportunity practices at the National Laboratories.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall develop and implement a strategy for facilities and infrastructure supported primarily from the Office of Science, the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy, the Office of Fossil Energy, or the Office of Nuclear Energy, Science and Technology Programs at all National Laboratories and single-purpose research facilities.

paragraph.heading: Strategy.—
paragraph.chapeau: The strategy shall provide cost-effective means for—

subparagraph.content: maintaining existing facilities and infrastructure;
closing unneeded facilities;
making facility modifications; and
building new facilities.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall prepare and submit, along with the budget request of the President submitted to Congress for fiscal year 2018, a report describing the strategy developed under subsection (a).

paragraph.heading: Contents.—
paragraph.chapeau: For each National Laboratory and single-purpose research facility that is primarily used for science and energy research, the report shall contain—

subparagraph.content: the current priority list of proposed facilities and infrastructure projects, including cost and schedule requirements;
a current 10-year plan that demonstrates the reconfiguration of its facilities and infrastructure to meet its missions and to address its long-term operational costs and return on investment;
the total current budget for all facilities and infrastructure funding; and
the current status of each facility and infrastructure project compared to the original baseline cost, schedule, and scope.

section.heading: STRATEGIC RESEARCH PORTFOLIO ANALYSIS AND COORDINATION PLAN.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall periodically review all of the science and technology activities of the Department in a strategic framework that takes into account—

paragraph.content: the frontiers of science to which the Department can contribute;
the national needs relevant to the statutory missions of the Department; and
global energy dynamics.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: As part of the review under subsection (a), the Secretary shall develop a plan to improve coordination and collaboration in research, development, demonstration, and commercial application activities across organizational boundaries of the Department.

paragraph.heading: Plan contents.—
paragraph.chapeau: The plan developed under paragraph (1) shall describe—

subparagraph.content: crosscutting scientific and technical issues and research questions that span more than one program or major office of the Department;
ways in which the applied technology programs of the Department are coordinating activities and addressing the questions referred to in subparagraph (A);

ways in which the technical interchange within the Department, particularly between the Office of Science and the applied technology programs, could be enhanced, including ways in which the research agendas of the Office of Science and the applied programs could better interact and assist each other;

ways in which the Secretary would ensure that the overall research agenda of the Department includes, in addition to fundamental, curiosity-driven research, fundamental research related to topics of concern to the applied programs, and applications in Departmental technology programs of research results generated by fundamental, curiosity-driven research;
critical assessments of any ongoing programs that have experienced subpar performance or cost overruns of 10 percent or more over 1 or more years;
any activities that may be more effectively left to the States, industry, nongovernmental organizations, institutions of higher education, or other stakeholders; and

subparagraph.chapeau: detailed evaluations and proposals for innovation hubs, institutes, and research centers of the Department, including—

clause.chapeau: an affirmation that the hubs, institutes, and research centers will—

subclause.content: advance the mission of the Department; and
prioritize research, development, and demonstration; and

clause.content: an affirmation that any hubs, institutes, or research centers that are established or renewed within the Office of Science are consistent with the mission of the Office of Science described in subsection (c) of section 209 of the Department of Energy Organization Act (42 U.S.C. 7139).

subsection.heading: Submission to Congress.—
subsection.chapeau: Every 4 years, the Secretary shall submit to Congress—

paragraph.content: the results of the review under subsection (a); and
the coordination plan under subsection (b).

section.heading: COMPETITIVE AWARD OF MANAGEMENT CONTRACTS.
section.content: None of the funds authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary by this title may be used to award a management and operating contract for a National Laboratory (excluding those named in subparagraphs (G), (H), (N), and (O) of section 2 (3)), unless such contract is competitively awarded, or the Secretary grants, on a case-by-case basis, a waiver. The Secretary may not delegate the authority to grant such a waiver and shall submit to Congress a report notifying it of the waiver, and setting forth the reasons for the waiver, at least 60 days prior to the date of the award of such contract.

section.heading: WESTERN MICHIGAN DEMONSTRATION PROJECT.
section.content: The Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, in consultation with the State of Michigan and affected local officials, shall conduct a demonstration project to address the effect of transported ozone and ozone precursors in Southwestern Michigan. The demonstration program shall address projected nonattainment areas in Southwestern Michigan that include counties with design values for ozone of less than .095 based on years 2000 to 2002 or the most current 3-year period of air quality data. The Administrator shall assess any difficulties such areas may experience in meeting the 8-hour national ambient air quality standard for ozone due to the effect of transported ozone or ozone precursors into the areas. The Administrator shall work with State and local officials to determine the extent of ozone and ozone precursor transport, to assess alternatives to achieve compliance with the 8-hour standard apart from local controls, and to determine the timeframe in which such compliance could take place. The Administrator shall complete this demonstration project no later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this section and shall not impose any requirement or sanction under the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7401 et seq.) that might otherwise apply during the pendency of the demonstration project.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of Transportation, in consultation with the Secretary and the United States Arctic Research Commission, shall provide annual grants to a university located adjacent to the Arctic Energy Office of the Department of Energy, to establish and operate a university research center to be headquartered in Fairbanks and to be known as the “Arctic Engineering Research Center” (referred to in this section as the “Center”).

subsection.heading: Purpose.—
subsection.chapeau: The purpose of the Center shall be to conduct research on, and develop improved methods of, construction and use of materials to improve the overall performance of roads, bridges, residential, commercial, and industrial structures, and other infrastructure in the Arctic region, with an emphasis on developing—

paragraph.content: new construction techniques for roads, bridges, rail, and related transportation infrastructure and residential, commercial, and industrial infrastructure that are capable of withstanding the Arctic environment and using limited energy resources as efficiently as practicable;

technologies and procedures for increasing road, bridge, rail, and related transportation infrastructure and residential, commercial, and industrial infrastructure safety, reliability, and integrity in the Arctic region;

new materials and improving the performance and energy efficiency of existing materials for the construction of roads, bridges, rail, and related transportation infrastructure and residential, commercial, and industrial infrastructure in the Arctic region; and

recommendations for new local, regional, and State permitting and building codes to ensure transportation and building safety and efficient energy use when constructing, using, and occupying such infrastructure in the Arctic region.

subsection.heading: Objectives.—
subsection.chapeau: The Center shall carry out—

paragraph.content: basic and applied research in the subjects described in subsection (b), the products of which shall be judged by peers or other experts in the field to advance the body of knowledge in road, bridge, rail, and infrastructure engineering in the Arctic region; and
an ongoing program of technology transfer that makes research results available to potential users in a form that can be implemented.

subsection.heading: Amount of Grant.—
subsection.content: For each of fiscal years 2006 through 2011, the Secretary shall provide a grant in the amount of $3,000,000 to the institution specified in subsection (a) to carry out this section.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $3,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2006 through 2011.

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretaries of Energy and the Interior, the Director of the National Science Foundation, and the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, shall establish a joint research facility in Barrow, Alaska, to be known as the “Barrow Geophysical Research Facility”, to support scientific research activities in the Arctic.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretaries of Commerce, Energy, and the Interior, the Director of the National Science Foundation, and the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency for the planning, design, construction, and support of the Barrow Geophysical Research Facility, $61,000,000.

subtitle.heading: Carbon Dioxide Transportation Infrastructure Finance and Innovation

paragraph.heading: CIFIA program.—
paragraph.content: The term “CIFIA program” means the carbon dioxide transportation infrastructure finance and innovation program established under section 999B(a).

paragraph.heading: Common carrier.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “common carrier” means a transportation infrastructure operator or owner that—

subparagraph.content: publishes a publicly available tariff containing the just and reasonable rates, terms, and conditions of nondiscriminatory service; and
holds itself out to provide transportation services to the public for a fee.

paragraph.heading: Contingent commitment.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “contingent commitment” means a commitment to obligate funds from future available budget authority that is—

subparagraph.content: contingent on those funds being made available in law at a future date; and
not an obligation of the Federal Government.

paragraph.heading: Eligible project costs.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “eligible project costs” means amounts substantially all of which are paid by, or for the account of, an obligor in connection with a project, including—

subparagraph.chapeau: the cost of—

clause.content: development-phase activities, including planning, feasibility analysis, revenue forecasting, environmental review, permitting, preliminary engineering and design work, and other preconstruction activities;

construction, reconstruction, rehabilitation, replacement, and acquisition of real property (including land relating to the project and improvements to land), environmental mitigation, construction contingencies, and acquisition and installation of equipment (including labor); and
capitalized interest necessary to meet market requirements, reasonably required reserve funds, capital issuance expenses, and other carrying costs during construction; and

subparagraph.chapeau: transaction costs associated with financing the project, including—

clause.content: the cost of legal counsel and technical consultants; and
any subsidy amount paid in accordance with section 999B(c)(3)(B)(ii) or section 999C(b)(6)(B)(ii).

paragraph.heading: Federal credit instrument.—
paragraph.content: The term “Federal credit instrument” means a secured loan or loan guarantee authorized to be provided under the CIFIA program with respect to a project.

paragraph.heading: Lender.—
paragraph.content: The term “lender” means a qualified institutional buyer (as defined in section 230.144A(a) of title 17, Code of Federal Regulations (or a successor regulation), commonly known as Rule 144A(a) of the Securities and Exchange Commission and issued under the Securities Act of 1933 (15 U.S.C. 77a et seq.)), that is not a Federal qualified institutional buyer.

paragraph.heading: Letter of interest.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “letter of interest” means a letter submitted by a potential applicant prior to an application for credit assistance in a format prescribed by the Secretary on the website of the CIFIA program that—

subparagraph.content: describes the project and the location, purpose, and cost of the project;
outlines the proposed financial plan, including the requested credit and grant assistance and the proposed obligor;
provides a status of environmental review; and
provides information regarding satisfaction of other eligibility requirements of the CIFIA program.

paragraph.heading: Loan guarantee.—
paragraph.content: The term “loan guarantee” means any guarantee or other pledge by the Secretary to pay all or part of the principal of, and interest on, a loan made to an obligor, or debt obligation issued by an obligor, in each case funded by a lender.

paragraph.heading: Master credit agreement.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “master credit agreement” means a conditional agreement that—

subparagraph.chapeau: is for the purpose of extending credit assistance for—

clause.content: a project of high priority under section 999B(c)(3)(A); or
a project covered under section 999B(c)(3)(B);

subparagraph.content: does not provide for a current obligation of Federal funds; and

subparagraph.chapeau: would—

clause.chapeau: make a contingent commitment of a Federal credit instrument or grant at a future date, subject to—

subclause.content: the availability of future funds being made available to carry out the CIFIA program; and
the satisfaction of all conditions for the provision of credit assistance under the CIFIA program, including section 999C(b);

clause.content: establish the maximum amounts and general terms and conditions of the Federal credit instruments or grants;
identify the 1 or more revenue sources that will secure the repayment of the Federal credit instruments;

clause.chapeau: provide for the obligation of funds for the Federal credit instruments or grants after all requirements have been met for the projects subject to the agreement, including—

subclause.content: compliance with all applicable requirements specified under the CIFIA program, including sections 999B(d) and 999C(b)(1); and
the availability of funds to carry out the CIFIA program; and

clause.content: require that contingent commitments shall result in a financial close and obligation of credit or grant assistance by not later than 4 years after the date of entry into the agreement or release of the commitment, as applicable, unless otherwise extended by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Obligor.—
paragraph.content: The term “obligor” means a corporation, partnership, joint venture, trust, non-Federal governmental entity, agency, or instrumentality, or other entity that is liable for payment of the principal of, or interest on, a Federal credit instrument.

paragraph.heading: Produced in the united states.—
paragraph.content: The term “produced in the United States”, with respect to iron and steel, means that all manufacturing processes for the iron and steel, including the application of any coating, occurs within the United States.

paragraph.heading: Project.—
paragraph.content: The term “project” means a project for common carrier carbon dioxide transportation infrastructure or associated equipment, including pipeline, shipping, rail, or other transportation infrastructure and associated equipment, that will transport or handle carbon dioxide captured from anthropogenic sources or ambient air, as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

paragraph.heading: Project obligation.—
paragraph.content: The term “project obligation” means any note, bond, debenture, or other debt obligation issued by an obligor in connection with the financing of a project, other than a Federal credit instrument.

paragraph.heading: Secured loan.—
paragraph.content: The term “secured loan” means a direct loan to an obligor or a debt obligation issued by an obligor and purchased by the Secretary, in each case funded by the Secretary in connection with the financing of a project under section 999C.

paragraph.heading: Subsidy amount.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “subsidy amount” means the amount of budget authority sufficient to cover the estimated long-term cost to the Federal Government of a Federal credit instrument—

subparagraph.content: calculated on a net present value basis; and
excluding administrative costs and any incidental effects on governmental receipts or outlays in accordance with the Federal Credit Reform Act of 1990 (2 U.S.C. 661 et seq.).

paragraph.heading: Substantial completion.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “substantial completion”, with respect to a project, means the date—

subparagraph.content: on which the project commences transportation of carbon dioxide; or
of a comparable event to the event described in subparagraph (A), as determined by the Secretary and specified in the project credit agreement.

section.heading: DETERMINATION OF ELIGIBILITY AND PROJECT SELECTION.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Program.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall establish and carry out a carbon dioxide transportation infrastructure finance and innovation program, under which the Secretary shall provide for eligible projects in accordance with this subtitle—

paragraph.content: a Federal credit instrument under section 999C;
a grant under section 999D; or
both a Federal credit instrument and a grant.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: A project shall be eligible to receive a Federal credit instrument or a grant under the CIFIA program if—

subparagraph.content: the entity proposing to carry out the project submits a letter of interest prior to submission of an application under paragraph (3) for the project; and
the project meets the criteria described in this subsection.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Each project and obligor that receives a Federal credit instrument or a grant under the CIFIA program shall be creditworthy, such that there exists a reasonable prospect of repayment of the principal and interest on the Federal credit instrument, as determined by the Secretary under subparagraph (B).

subparagraph.heading: Reasonable prospect of repayment.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall base a determination of whether there is a reasonable prospect of repayment under subparagraph (A) on a comprehensive evaluation of whether the obligor has a reasonable prospect of repaying the Federal credit instrument for the eligible project, including evaluation of—

clause.content: the strength of the contractual terms of an eligible project (if available for the applicable market segment);
the forecast of noncontractual cash flows supported by market projections from reputable sources, as determined by the Secretary, and cash sweeps or other structural enhancements;

clause.chapeau: the projected financial strength of the obligor—

subclause.content: at the time of loan close; and
throughout the loan term, including after the project is completed;

clause.content: the financial strength of the investors and strategic partners of the obligor, if applicable; and
other financial metrics and analyses that are relied on by the private lending community and nationally recognized credit rating agencies, as determined appropriate by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Applications.—
paragraph.content: To be eligible for assistance under the CIFIA program, an obligor shall submit to the Secretary a project application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

paragraph.heading: Eligible project costs.—
paragraph.content: A project under the CIFIA program shall have eligible project costs that are reasonably anticipated to equal or exceed $100,000,000.

paragraph.heading: Revenue sources.—
paragraph.chapeau: The applicable Federal credit instrument shall be repayable, in whole or in part, from—

subparagraph.content: user fees;
payments owing to the obligor under a public-private partnership; or
other revenue sources that also secure or fund the project obligations.

paragraph.heading: Obligor will be identified later.—
paragraph.chapeau: A State, local government, agency, or instrumentality of a State or local government, or a public authority, may submit to the Secretary an application under paragraph (3), under which a private party to a public-private partnership will be—

subparagraph.content: the obligor; and
identified at a later date through completion of a procurement and selection of the private party.

paragraph.heading: Beneficial effects.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall determine that financial assistance for each project under the CIFIA program will—

subparagraph.content: attract public or private investment for the project; or
enable the project to proceed at an earlier date than the project would otherwise be able to proceed or reduce the lifecycle costs (including debt service costs) of the project.

paragraph.heading: Project readiness.—
paragraph.content: To be eligible for assistance under the CIFIA program, the applicant shall demonstrate a reasonable expectation that the contracting process for construction of the project can commence by not later than 90 days after the date on which a Federal credit instrument or grant is obligated for the project under the CIFIA program.

paragraph.heading: Establishment of application process.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall establish an application process under which projects that are eligible to receive assistance under subsection (b) may—

subparagraph.content: receive credit assistance on terms acceptable to the Secretary, if adequate funds are available (including any funds provided on behalf of an eligible project under paragraph (3)(B)(ii)) to cover the subsidy amount associated with the Federal credit instrument; and

subparagraph.chapeau: receive grants under section 999D if—

clause.content: adequate funds are available to cover the amount of the grant; and
the Secretary determines that the project is eligible under subsection (b).

paragraph.heading: Priority.—
paragraph.chapeau: In selecting projects to receive credit assistance under subsection (b), the Secretary shall give priority to projects that—

subparagraph.content: are large-capacity, common carrier infrastructure;
have demonstrated demand for use of the infrastructure by associated projects that capture carbon dioxide from anthropogenic sources or ambient air;

enable geographical diversity in associated projects that capture carbon dioxide from anthropogenic sources or ambient air, with the goal of enabling projects in all major carbon dioxide-emitting regions of the United States; and
are sited within, or adjacent to, existing pipeline or other linear infrastructure corridors, in a manner that minimizes environmental disturbance and other siting concerns.

subparagraph.heading: Priority projects.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary may enter into a master credit agreement for a project that the Secretary determines—

clause.chapeau: will likely be eligible for credit assistance under subsection (b), on obtaining—

subclause.content: additional commitments from associated carbon capture projects to use the project; or
all necessary permits and approvals; and

clause.content: is a project of high priority, as determined in accordance with the criteria described in paragraph (2).

subparagraph.heading: Adequate funding not available.—
subparagraph.chapeau: If the Secretary fully obligates funding to eligible projects for a fiscal year and adequate funding is not available to fund a Federal credit instrument, a project sponsor (including a unit of State or local government) of an eligible project may elect—

subclause.content: to enter into a master credit agreement in lieu of the Federal credit instrument; and
to wait to execute a Federal credit instrument until the fiscal year for which additional funds are available to receive credit assistance; or

clause.content: if the lack of adequate funding is solely with respect to amounts available for the subsidy amount, to pay the subsidy amount to fund the Federal credit instrument.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Nothing in this subtitle supersedes the applicability of any other requirement under Federal law (including regulations).

paragraph.heading: NEPA.—
paragraph.content: Federal credit assistance may only be provided under this subtitle for a project that has received an environmental categorical exclusion, a finding of no significant impact, or a record of decision under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (42 U.S.C. 4321 et seq.).

subsection.heading: Use of American Iron, Steel, and Manufactured Goods.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Except as provided in paragraph (2), no Federal credit instrument or grant provided under the CIFIA program shall be made available for a project unless all iron, steel, and manufactured goods used in the project are produced in the United States.

paragraph.heading: Exceptions.—
paragraph.chapeau: Paragraph (1) shall not apply in any case or category of cases with respect to which the Secretary determines that—

subparagraph.content: the application would be inconsistent with the public interest;
iron, steel, or a relevant manufactured good is not produced in the United States in sufficient and reasonably available quantity, or of a satisfactory quality; or
the inclusion of iron, steel, or a manufactured good produced in the United States will increase the cost of the overall project by more than 25 percent.

paragraph.heading: Waivers.—
paragraph.chapeau: If the Secretary receives a request for a waiver under this subsection, the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.chapeau: make available to the public a copy of the request, together with any information available to the Secretary concerning the request—

clause.content: on an informal basis; and
by electronic means, including on the official public website of the Department;

subparagraph.content: allow for informal public comment relating to the request for not fewer than 15 days before making a determination with respect to the request; and
approve or disapprove the request by not later than the date that is 120 days after the date of receipt of the request.

paragraph.heading: Applicability.—
paragraph.content: This subsection shall be applied in accordance with any applicable obligations of the United States under international agreements.

paragraph.heading: Notice of complete application.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 30 days after the date of receipt of an application under this section, the Secretary shall provide to the applicant a written notice describing whether—

subparagraph.content: the application is complete; or
additional information or materials are needed to complete the application.

paragraph.heading: Approval or denial of application.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 60 days after the date of issuance of a written notice under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall provide to the applicant a written notice informing the applicant whether the Secretary has approved or disapproved the application.

subsection.heading: Development-phase Activities.—
subsection.content: Any Federal credit instrument provided under the CIFIA program may be used to finance up to 100 percent of the cost of development-phase activities, as described in section 999A(4)(A).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Subject to paragraph (2), the Secretary may enter into agreements with 1 or more obligors to make secured loans, the proceeds of which—

subparagraph.chapeau: shall be used—

clause.content: to finance eligible project costs of any project selected under section 999B;
to refinance interim construction financing of eligible project costs of any project selected under section 999B; or

clause.chapeau: to refinance long-term project obligations or Federal credit instruments, if the refinancing provides additional funding capacity for the completion, enhancement, or expansion of any project that—

subclause.content: is selected under section 999B; or
otherwise meets the requirements of that section; and

subparagraph.content: may be used in accordance with subsection (b)(7) to pay any fees collected by the Secretary under subparagraph (B) of that subsection.

paragraph.heading: Risk assessment.—
paragraph.content: Before entering into an agreement under this subsection, the Secretary, in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, shall determine an appropriate credit subsidy amount for each secured loan, taking into account all relevant factors, including the creditworthiness factors under section 999B(b)(2).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: A secured loan under this section with respect to a project shall be on such terms and conditions and contain such covenants, representations, warranties, and requirements (including requirements for audits) as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

paragraph.heading: Maximum amount.—
paragraph.content: The amount of a secured loan under this section shall not exceed an amount equal to 80 percent of the reasonably anticipated eligible project costs.

paragraph.heading: Payment.—
paragraph.chapeau: A secured loan under this section shall be payable, in whole or in part, from—

subparagraph.content: user fees;
payments owing to the obligor under a public-private partnership; or
other revenue sources that also secure or fund the project obligations.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Except as provided in subparagraph (B), the interest rate on a secured loan under this section shall be not less than the interest rate reflected in the yield on United States Treasury securities of a similar maturity to the maturity of the secured loan on the date of execution of the loan agreement.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.chapeau: Subject to clause (iii), the Secretary may lower the interest rate of a secured loan under this section to not lower than the interest rate described in clause (ii), if the interest rate has increased during the period—

item.content: the date on which an application acceptable to the Secretary is submitted for the applicable project; or
the date on which the Secretary entered into a master credit agreement for the applicable project; and

subclause.content: ending on the date on which the Secretary executes the Federal credit instrument for the applicable project that is the subject of the secured loan.

clause.heading: Description of interest rate.—
clause.chapeau: The interest rate referred to in clause (i) is the interest rate reflected in the yield on United States Treasury securities of a similar maturity to the maturity of the secured loan in effect, as applicable to the project that is the subject of the secured loan, on—

subclause.content: the date described in clause (i)(I)(aa); or
the date described in clause (i)(I)(bb).

clause.heading: Limitation.—
clause.content: The interest rate of a secured loan may not be lowered pursuant to clause (i) by more than 1½ percentage points (150 basis points).

paragraph.heading: Maturity date.—
paragraph.chapeau: The final maturity date of the secured loan shall be the earlier of—

subparagraph.content: the date that is 35 years after the date of substantial completion of the project; and
if the useful life of the capital asset being financed is of a lesser period, the date that is the end of the useful life of the asset.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Except as provided in subparagraph (B), the secured loan shall not be subordinated to the claims of any holder of project obligations in the event of bankruptcy, insolvency, or liquidation of the obligor.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.chapeau: The Secretary shall waive the requirement under subparagraph (A) for a public agency borrower that is financing ongoing capital programs and has outstanding senior bonds under a preexisting indenture, if—

subclause.content: the secured loan is rated in the A category or higher; and
the secured loan is secured and payable from pledged revenues not affected by project performance, such as a tax-backed revenue pledge or a system-backed pledge of project revenues.

clause.heading: Limitation.—
clause.chapeau: If the Secretary waives the nonsubordination requirement under this subparagraph—

subclause.content: the maximum credit subsidy amount to be paid by the Federal Government shall be not more than 10 percent of the principal amount of the secured loan; and
the obligor shall be responsible for paying the remainder of the subsidy amount, if any.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary may collect a fee on or after the date of the financial close of a Federal credit instrument under this section in an amount equal to not more than $3,000,000 to cover all or a portion of the costs to the Federal Government of providing the Federal credit instrument.

subparagraph.heading: Amendment to add cost of fees to secured loan.—
subparagraph.content: If the Secretary collects a fee from an obligor under subparagraph (A) to cover all or a portion of the costs to the Federal Government of providing a secured loan, the obligor and the Secretary may amend the terms of the secured loan to add to the principal of the secured loan an amount equal to the amount of the fee collected by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Maximum federal involvement.—
paragraph.content: The total Federal assistance provided for a project under the CIFIA program, including any grant provided under section 999D, shall not exceed an amount equal to 80 percent of the eligible project costs.

paragraph.heading: Schedule.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall establish a repayment schedule for each secured loan under this section based on—

subparagraph.content: the projected cash flow from project revenues and other repayment sources; and
the useful life of the project.

paragraph.heading: Commencement.—
paragraph.content: Scheduled loan repayments of principal or interest on a secured loan under this section shall commence not later than 5 years after the date of substantial completion of the project.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: If, at any time after the date of substantial completion of a project, the project is unable to generate sufficient revenues in excess of reasonable and necessary operating expenses to pay the scheduled loan repayments of principal and interest on the secured loan, the Secretary may, subject to subparagraph (C), allow the obligor to add unpaid principal and interest to the outstanding balance of the secured loan.

subparagraph.heading: Interest.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Any payment deferred under subparagraph (A) shall—

clause.content: continue to accrue interest in accordance with subsection (b)(4) until fully repaid; and
be scheduled to be amortized over the remaining term of the loan.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Any payment deferral under subparagraph (A) shall be contingent on the project meeting criteria established by the Secretary.

clause.heading: Repayment standards.—
clause.content: The criteria established pursuant to clause (i) shall include standards for the reasonable prospect of repayment.

subparagraph.heading: Use of excess revenues.—
subparagraph.content: Any excess revenues that remain after satisfying scheduled debt service requirements on the project obligations and secured loan and all deposit requirements under the terms of any trust agreement, bond resolution, or similar agreement securing project obligations may be applied annually to prepay the secured loan, without penalty.

subparagraph.heading: Use of proceeds of refinancing.—
subparagraph.content: A secured loan may be prepaid at any time without penalty from the proceeds of refinancing from non-Federal funding sources.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Subject to paragraph (2), as soon as practicable after substantial completion of a project and after notifying the obligor, the Secretary may sell to another entity or reoffer into the capital markets a secured loan for the project if the Secretary determines that the sale or reoffering can be made on favorable terms.

paragraph.heading: Consent of obligor.—
paragraph.content: In making a sale or reoffering under paragraph (1), the Secretary may not change any original term or condition of the secured loan without the written consent of the obligor.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may provide a loan guarantee to a lender in lieu of making a secured loan under this section if the Secretary determines that the budgetary cost of the loan guarantee is substantially the same as, or less than, that of a secured loan.

paragraph.heading: Terms.—
paragraph.content: The terms of a loan guarantee under paragraph (1) shall be consistent with the terms required under this section for a secured loan, except that the rate on the guaranteed loan and any prepayment features shall be negotiated between the obligor and the lender, with the consent of the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Establishment.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary may provide grants to pay a portion of the cost differential, with respect to any projected future increase in demand for carbon dioxide transportation by an infrastructure project described in subsection (b), between—

paragraph.content: the cost of constructing the infrastructure asset with the capacity to transport an increased flow rate of carbon dioxide, as made practicable under the project; and
the cost of constructing the infrastructure asset with the capacity to transport carbon dioxide at the flow rate initially required, based on commitments for the use of the asset.

subsection.heading: Eligibility.—
subsection.chapeau: To be eligible to receive a grant under this section, an entity shall—

paragraph.content: be eligible to receive credit assistance under the CIFIA program;
carry out, or propose to carry out, a project for large-capacity, common carrier infrastructure with a probable future increase in demand for carbon dioxide transportation; and
submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

subsection.heading: Use of Funds.—
subsection.content: A grant provided under this section may be used only to pay the costs of any additional flow rate capacity of a carbon dioxide transportation infrastructure asset that the project sponsor demonstrates to the satisfaction of the Secretary can reasonably be expected to be used during the 20-year period beginning on the date of substantial completion of the project described in subsection (b)(2).

subsection.heading: Maximum Amount.—
subsection.content: The amount of a grant provided under this section may not exceed an amount equal to 80 percent of the cost of the additional capacity described in subsection (a).

subsection.heading: Requirement.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall establish a uniform system to service the Federal credit instruments provided under the CIFIA program.

subsection.heading: Fees.—
subsection.content: If funding sufficient to cover the costs of services of expert firms retained pursuant to subsection (d) and all or a portion of the costs to the Federal Government of servicing the Federal credit instruments is not provided in an appropriations Act for a fiscal year, the Secretary, during that fiscal year, may collect fees on or after the date of the financial close of a Federal credit instrument provided under the CIFIA program at a level that is sufficient to cover those costs.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may appoint a financial entity to assist the Secretary in servicing the Federal credit instruments.

paragraph.heading: Duties.—
paragraph.content: A servicer appointed under paragraph (1) shall act as the agent for the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Fee.—
paragraph.content: A servicer appointed under paragraph (1) shall receive a servicing fee, subject to approval by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Assistance From Expert Firms.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may retain the services of expert firms, including counsel, in the field of municipal and project finance to assist in the underwriting and servicing of Federal credit instruments.

subsection.heading: Expedited Processing.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall implement procedures and measures to economize the time and cost involved in obtaining approval and the issuance of credit assistance under the CIFIA program.

section.heading: STATE AND LOCAL PERMITS.
section.chapeau: The provision of credit assistance under the CIFIA program with respect to a project shall not—

paragraph.content: relieve any recipient of the assistance of any project obligation to obtain any required State or local permit or approval with respect to the project;
limit the right of any unit of State or local government to approve or regulate any rate of return on private equity invested in the project; or
otherwise supersede any State or local law (including any regulation) applicable to the construction or operation of the project.

section.heading: REGULATIONS.
section.content: The Secretary may promulgate such regulations as the Secretary determines to be appropriate to carry out the CIFIA program.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this subtitle—

subparagraph.content: $600,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2022 and 2023; and
$300,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2024 through 2026.

paragraph.heading: Spending and borrowing authority.—
paragraph.content: Spending and borrowing authority for a fiscal year to enter into Federal credit instruments shall be promptly apportioned to the Secretary on a fiscal-year basis.

paragraph.heading: Reestimates.—
paragraph.content: If the subsidy amount of a Federal credit instrument is reestimated, the cost increase or decrease of the reestimate shall be borne by, or benefit, the general fund of the Treasury, consistent with section 504(f) of the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 (2 U.S.C. 661c(f)).

paragraph.heading: Administrative costs.—
paragraph.content: Of the amounts made available to carry out the CIFIA program, the Secretary may use not more than $9,000,000 (as indexed for United States dollar inflation from the date of enactment of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (as measured by the Consumer Price Index)) each fiscal year for the administration of the CIFIA program.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, execution of a term sheet by the Secretary of a Federal credit instrument that uses amounts made available under the CIFIA program shall impose on the United States a contractual obligation to fund the Federal credit investment.

paragraph.heading: Availability.—
paragraph.content: Amounts made available to carry out the CIFIA program for a fiscal year shall be available for obligation on October 1 of the fiscal year.

section.heading: IMPROVED TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER OF ENERGY TECHNOLOGIES.

paragraph.heading: Establishment.—
paragraph.content: There is established within the Department an Office of Technology Transitions (referred to in this section as the “Office”).

paragraph.heading: Mission.—
paragraph.chapeau: The mission of the Office shall be—

subparagraph.content: to expand the commercial impact of the research investments of the Department; and
to focus on commercializing technologies that support the missions of the Department, including reducing greenhouse gas emissions and other pollutants.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: In carrying out the mission and activities of the Office, the Chief Commercialization Officer appointed under paragraph (4) shall, with respect to commercialization activities, meet all of the goals described in subparagraph (B).

subparagraph.heading: Goals described.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The goals referred to in subparagraph (A) are the following:

clause.content: Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and other pollutants.
Ensuring economic competitiveness.
Enhancement of domestic energy security and national security.
Enhancement of domestic jobs.
Improvement of energy efficiency.
Any other goals to support the transfer of technology developed by Department-funded programs to the private sector, as consistent with missions of the Department.

subparagraph.heading: In general
subparagraph.content: The Office shall be headed by an officer, who shall be known as the “Chief Commercialization Officer”, and who shall report directly to, and be appointed by, the Secretary.

subparagraph.heading: Principal advisor
subparagraph.content: The Chief Commercialization Officer shall be the principal advisor to the Secretary on all matters relating to technology transfer and commercialization.

subparagraph.heading: Qualifications.—
subparagraph.content: The Chief Commercialization Officer shall be an individual who, by reason of professional background and experience, is specially qualified to advise the Secretary on matters pertaining to technology transfer at the Department.

subparagraph.heading: Duties.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Chief Commercialization Officershall oversee—

clause.content: the activities of the Technology Transfer Working Group established under subsection (b);
the expenditure of funds allocated for technology transfer within the Department;
the activities of each technology partnership ombudsman appointed under section 11 of the Technology Transfer Commercialization Act of 2000 (42 U.S.C. 7261c); and
efforts to engage private sector entities, including venture capital companies.

paragraph.heading: Coordination.—
paragraph.content: In carrying out the mission and activities of the Office, the Chief Commercialization Officer shall coordinate with the senior leadership of the Department, other relevant program offices of the Department, National Laboratories, the Technology Transfer Working Group established under subsection (b), the Technology Transfer Policy Board, and other stakeholders (including private industry).

paragraph.heading: Hiring and management.—
paragraph.content: To carry out the program authorized in this section, the Under Secretary for Science may appoint personnel using the authorities in section 10726 of the Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act.

paragraph.heading: Authorization of appropriations.—
paragraph.content: There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out the activities authorized in this section $20,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2023 through 2027.

subsection.heading: Technology Transfer Working Group.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall establish a Technology Transfer Working Group, which shall consist of representatives of the National Laboratories and single-purpose research facilities, to—

paragraph.content: coordinate technology transfer activities occurring at National Laboratories and single-purpose research facilities;
exchange information about technology transfer practices, including alternative approaches to resolution of disputes involving intellectual property rights and other technology transfer matters; and

develop and disseminate to the public and prospective technology partners information about opportunities and procedures for technology transfer with the Department, including opportunities and procedures related to alternative approaches to resolution of disputes involving intellectual property rights and other technology transfer matters.

subsection.heading: Technology Commercialization Fund.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall establish an Energy Technology Commercialization Fund, using 0.9 percent of the amount made available to the Department for applied energy research, development, demonstration, and commercial application for each fiscal year based on future planned activities and the amount of the appropriations for the fiscal year, to be used to provide matching funds with private partners to promote promising energy technologies for commercial purposes.

subsection.heading: Technology Transfer Responsibility.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section affects the technology transfer responsibilities of Federal employees under the Stevenson-Wydler Technology Innovation Act of 1980 (15 U.S.C. 3701 et seq.).

paragraph.heading: Establishment.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary, acting through the Chief Commercialization Officer established in section 1001(a) of the Energy Policy Act of 2005 (42 U.S.C. 16391(a)), shall establish a Technology Commercialization Fund (hereafter referred to as the “Fund”), using nine-tenths of one percent of the amount of appropriations made available to the Department for applied energy research, development, demonstration, and commercial application for each fiscal year, to be used to provide, in accordance with the cost-sharing requirements under section 988, funds to private partners, including national laboratories, to promote promising energy technologies for commercial purposes.

subparagraph.heading: Considerations.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall develop criteria for evaluating applications for funding under this section, which may include—

clause.content: the potential that a proposed technology will result in a commercially successful product within a reasonable timeframe; and
the relative maturity of a proposed technology for commercial application.

subparagraph.heading: Selections.—
subparagraph.content: In awarding funds under this section, the Secretary may give special consideration to applications that involve at least one applicant that has participated in an entrepreneurial or commercialization training program, such as Energy Innovation Corps.

subsection.heading: Annual Report.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall include in the annual report required under section 9007(a) of the Energy Act of 2020—

paragraph.content: description of the projects carried out with awards from the Fund for that fiscal year;
each project’s cost-share for that fiscal year; and
each project’s partners for that fiscal year.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of the Energy Act of 2020, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology and Committee on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources and Committee on Appropriations of the Senate a report on the current and recommended implementation of the Fund.

paragraph.heading: Contents.—
paragraph.chapeau: The report under subparagraph (A) shall include—

subparagraph.content: a summary, with supporting data, of how much Department program offices contribute to and use the Fund each year, including a list of current funding restrictions;
recommendations on how to improve implementation and administration of the Fund; and

an analysis on how to spend funds optimally on technology areas that have the greatest need and opportunity for commercial application, rather than spending funds at the programmatic level or under current funding restrictions.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a technology transfer execution plan.

paragraph.heading: Updates.—
paragraph.content: Each year after the submission of the plan under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall submit to Congress an updated execution plan and reports that describe progress toward meeting goals set forth in the execution plan and the funds expended under subsection (c).

subsection.heading: Additional Technology Transfer Programs.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary may develop additional programs to—
