paragraph.content: The Secretary and the Secretary of the Interior (referred to in this section as the “Secretaries”) shall jointly conduct a study of issues regarding energy rights-of-way on tribal land (as defined in section 2601 of the Energy Policy Act of 1992 (as amended by section 503)) (referred to in this section as “tribal land”).

paragraph.heading: Consultation.—
paragraph.content: In conducting the study under paragraph (1), the Secretaries shall consult with Indian tribes, the energy industry, appropriate governmental entities, and affected businesses and consumers.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretaries shall submit to Congress a report on the findings of the study, including—

paragraph.content: an analysis of historic rates of compensation paid for energy rights-of-way on tribal land;

recommendations for appropriate standards and procedures for determining fair and appropriate compensation to Indian tribes for grants, expansions, and renewals of energy rights-of-way on tribal land;
an assessment of the tribal self-determination and sovereignty interests implicated by applications for the grant, expansion, or renewal of energy rights-of-way on tribal land; and
an analysis of relevant national energy transportation policies relating to grants, expansions, and renewals of energy rights-of-way on tribal land.

section.heading: MOBILITY OF SCIENTIFIC AND TECHNICAL PERSONNEL.

subsection.chapeau: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this section, the Secretary shall transmit to Congress a report that—

paragraph.content: identifies any policies or procedures of a contractor operating a National Laboratory or single-purpose research facility that create disincentives to the temporary or permanent transfer of scientific and technical personnel among the contractor-operated National Laboratories or contractor-operated single-purpose research facilities; and
provides recommendations for improving interlaboratory exchange of scientific and technical personnel.

section.heading: INTERAGENCY REVIEW OF COMPETITION IN THE WHOLESALE AND RETAIL MARKETS FOR ELECTRIC ENERGY.

subsection.heading: Task Force.—
subsection.chapeau: There is established an inter-agency task force, to be known as the “Electric Energy Market Competition Task Force” (referred to in this section as the “task force”), consisting of five members—

paragraph.content: one of whom shall be an employee of the Department of Justice, to be appointed by the Attorney General of the United States;
one of whom shall be an employee of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, to be appointed by the Chairperson of that Commission;
one of whom shall be an employee of the Federal Trade Commission, to be appointed by the Chairperson of that Commission;
one of whom shall be an employee of the Department, to be appointed by the Secretary; and
one of whom shall be an employee of the Rural Utilities Service, to be appointed by the Secretary of Agriculture.

paragraph.heading: Study.—
paragraph.content: The task force shall conduct a study and analysis of competition within the wholesale and retail market for electric energy in the United States.

subparagraph.heading: Final report.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the task force shall submit to Congress a final report on the findings of the task force under paragraph (1).

subparagraph.heading: Public comment.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not later than the date that is 60 days before a final report is submitted to Congress under subparagraph (A), the task force shall—

clause.content: publish in the Federal Register a draft of the report; and
provide an opportunity for public comment on the report.

subsection.heading: Consultation.—
subsection.content: In conducting the study under subsection (b), the task force shall consult with and solicit comments from any advisory entity of the task force, the States, representatives of the electric power industry, and the public.

section.heading: STUDY OF RAPID ELECTRICAL GRID RESTORATION.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall conduct a study of the benefits of using mobile transformers and mobile substations to rapidly restore electrical service to areas subjected to blackouts as a result of—

subparagraph.content: equipment failure;
natural disasters;
acts of terrorism; or
war.

paragraph.heading: Contents.—
paragraph.chapeau: The study under paragraph (1) shall contain an analysis of—

subparagraph.content: the feasibility of using mobile transformers and mobile substations to reduce dependence on foreign entities for key elements of the electrical grid system of the United States;

subparagraph.chapeau: the feasibility of using mobile transformers and mobile substations to rapidly restore electrical power to—

clause.content: military bases;
the Federal Government;
communications industries;
first responders; and
other critical infrastructures, as determined by the Secretary;

subparagraph.chapeau: the quantity of mobile transformers and mobile substations necessary—

clause.content: to eliminate dependence on foreign sources for key electrical grid components in the United States;
to rapidly deploy technology to fully restore full electrical service to prioritized Governmental functions; and

to identify manufacturing sources in existence on the date of enactment of this Act that have previously manufactured specialized mobile transformer or mobile substation products for Federal agencies.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the President and Congress a report on the study under subsection (a).

paragraph.heading: Inclusion.—
paragraph.content: The report shall include a description of the results of the analysis under subsection (a)(2).

subparagraph.heading: Potential benefits.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary, in consultation with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, shall conduct a study of the potential benefits of cogeneration and small power production.

subparagraph.heading: Recipients.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The benefits described in subparagraph (A) include benefits that are received directly or indirectly by—

clause.content: an electricity distribution or transmission service provider;
other customers served by an electricity distribution or transmission service provider; and
the general public in the area served by the public utility in which the cogenerator or small power producer is located.

paragraph.heading: Inclusions.—
paragraph.chapeau: The study shall include an analysis of—

subparagraph.chapeau: the potential benefits of—

clause.content: increased system reliability;
improved power quality;
the provision of ancillary services;
reduction of peak power requirements through onsite generation;
the provision of reactive power or volt-ampere reactives;
an emergency supply of power;
offsets to investments in generation, transmission, or distribution facilities that would otherwise be recovered through rates;
diminished land use effects and right-of-way acquisition costs; and
reducing the vulnerability of a system to terrorism; and

subparagraph.content: any rate-related issue that may impede or otherwise discourage the expansion of cogeneration and small power production facilities, including a review of whether rates, rules, or other requirements imposed on the facilities are comparable to rates imposed on customers of the same class that do not have cogeneration or small power production.

paragraph.heading: Valuation of benefits.—
paragraph.content: In carrying out the study, the Secretary shall determine an appropriate method of valuing potential benefits under varying circumstances for individual cogeneration or small power production units.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 18 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall—

paragraph.content: complete the study;
provide an opportunity for public comment on the results of the study; and

paragraph.chapeau: submit to the President and Congress a report describing—

subparagraph.content: the results of the study; and
information relating to the public comments received under paragraph (2).

subsection.heading: Publication.—
subsection.content: After submission of the report under subsection (b) to the President and Congress, the Secretary shall publish the report.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report on natural gas supplies and demand.

subsection.heading: Purpose.—
subsection.chapeau: The purpose of the report under subsection (a) is to develop recommendations for achieving a balance between natural gas supply and demand in order to—

paragraph.content: provide residential consumers with natural gas at reasonable and stable prices;
accommodate long-term maintenance and growth of domestic natural gas-dependent industrial, manufacturing, and commercial enterprises;
facilitate the attainment of national ambient air quality standards under the Clean Air Act (43 U.S.C. 7401 et seq.);
achieve continued progress in reducing the emissions associated with electric power generation; and
support the development of the preliminary phases of hydrogen-based energy technologies.

subsection.heading: Comprehensive Analysis.—
subsection.chapeau: The report shall include a comprehensive analysis of, for the period beginning on January 1, 2004, and ending on December 31, 2015, natural gas supply and demand in the United States, including—

paragraph.content: estimates of annual domestic demand for natural gas, taking into consideration the effect of Federal policies and actions that are likely to increase or decrease the demand for natural gas;
projections of annual natural gas supplies, from domestic and foreign sources, under Federal policies in existence on the date of enactment of this Act;
an identification of estimated natural gas supplies that are not available under those Federal policies;

paragraph.chapeau: scenarios for decreasing natural gas demand and increasing natural gas supplies that compare the relative economic and environmental impacts of Federal policies that—

subparagraph.content: encourage or require the use of natural gas to meet air quality, carbon dioxide emission reduction, or energy security goals;
encourage or require the use of energy sources other than natural gas, including coal, nuclear, and renewable sources;
support technologies to develop alternative sources of natural gas and synthetic gas, including coal gasification technologies;
encourage or require the use of energy conservation and demand side management practices; and
affect access to domestic natural gas supplies; and

paragraph.chapeau: recommendations for Federal actions to achieve the purposes described in subsection (b), including recommendations that—

subparagraph.content: encourage or require the use of energy sources other than natural gas, including coal, nuclear, and renewable sources;
encourage or require the use of energy conservation or demand side management practices;
support technologies for the development of alternative sources of natural gas and synthetic gas, including coal gasification technologies; and
would improve access to domestic natural gas supplies.

subsection.heading: Consultation.—
subsection.chapeau: In preparing the report under subsection (a), the Secretary shall consult with—

paragraph.content: experts in natural gas supply and demand; and

paragraph.chapeau: representatives of—

subparagraph.content: State and local governments;
tribal organizations; and
consumer and other organizations.

subsection.heading: Hearings.—
subsection.content: In preparing the report under subsection (a), the Secretary may hold public hearings and provide other opportunities for public comment, as the Secretary considers appropriate.

section.heading: HYDROGEN PARTICIPATION STUDY.
section.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report evaluating methodologies to ensure the widest participation practicable in setting goals and milestones under the hydrogen program of the Department, including international participants.

section.heading: OVERALL EMPLOYMENT IN A HYDROGEN ECONOMY.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall carry out a study of the likely effects of a transition to a hydrogen economy on overall employment in the United States.

paragraph.heading: Contents.—
paragraph.chapeau: In completing the study, the Secretary shall take into consideration—

subparagraph.content: the replacement effects of new goods and services;
international competition;
workforce training requirements;
multiple possible fuel cycles, including usage of raw materials;
rates of market penetration of technologies; and
regional variations based on geography.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.content: Not later than 18 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report describing the findings, conclusions, and recommendations of the study under subsection (a).

section.heading: STUDY OF BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES FOR ENERGY RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall enter into an arrangement with the National Academy of Public Administration under which the Academy shall conduct a study to assess management practices for research, development, and demonstration programs at the Department.

subsection.heading: Scope of the Study.—
subsection.chapeau: The study shall consider—

paragraph.content: management practices that act as barriers between the Office of Science and offices conducting mission-oriented research;
recommendations for management practices that would improve coordination and bridge the innovation gap between the Office of Science and offices conducting mission-oriented research;
the applicability of the management practices used by the Department of Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency to research programs at the Department;
the advisability of creating an agency within the Department modeled after the Department of Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency;
recommendations for management practices that could best encourage innovative research and efficiency at the Department; and
any other relevant considerations.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.content: Not later than 18 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report on the study conducted under this section.

section.heading: EFFECT OF ELECTRICAL CONTAMINANTS ON RELIABILITY OF ENERGY PRODUCTION SYSTEMS.
section.content: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall enter into a contract with the National Academy of Sciences under which the National Academy of Sciences shall determine the effect that electrical contaminants (such as tin whiskers) may have on the reliability of energy production systems, including nuclear energy.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to Congress reports on the potential for each of biodiesel and hythane to become major, sustainable, alternative fuels.

subsection.heading: Biodiesel Report.—
subsection.chapeau: The report relating to biodiesel submitted under subsection (a) shall—

paragraph.chapeau: provide a detailed assessment of—

subparagraph.content: potential biodiesel markets and manufacturing capacity; and
environmental and energy security benefits with respect to the use of biodiesel;

paragraph.content: identify any impediments, especially in infrastructure needed for production, distribution, and storage, to biodiesel becoming a substantial source of fuel for conventional diesel and heating oil applications;
identify strategies to enhance the commercial deployment of biodiesel; and
include an examination and recommendations, as appropriate, of the ways in which biodiesel may be modified to be a cleaner-burning fuel.

subsection.heading: Hythane Report.—
subsection.chapeau: The report relating to hythane submitted under subsection (a) shall—

paragraph.content: provide a detailed assessment of potential hythane markets and the research and development activities that are necessary to facilitate the commercialization of hythane as a competitive, environmentally friendly transportation fuel;

paragraph.chapeau: address—

subparagraph.content: the infrastructure necessary to produce, blend, distribute, and store hythane for widespread commercial purposes; and
other potential market barriers to the commercialization of hythane;

paragraph.content: examine the viability of producing hydrogen using energy-efficient, environmentally friendly methods so that the hydrogen can be blended with natural gas to produce hythane; and
include an assessment of the modifications that would be required to convert compressed natural gas vehicle engines to engines that use hythane as fuel.

subsection.heading: Grants for Report Completion.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may use such sums as are available to the Secretary to provide, to one or more colleges or universities selected by the Secretary, grants for use in carrying out research to assist the Secretary in preparing the reports required to be submitted under subsection (a).

section.heading: FINAL ACTION ON REFUNDS FOR EXCESSIVE CHARGES.

subsection.chapeau: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) shall—

paragraph.content: seek to conclude its investigation into the unjust or unreasonable charges incurred by California during the 2000–2001 electricity crisis as soon as possible;
seek to ensure that refunds the Commission determines are owed to the State of California are paid to the State of California; and
submit to Congress a report by December 31, 2005, describing the actions taken by the Commission to date under this section and timetables for further actions.

section.heading: FUEL CELL AND HYDROGEN TECHNOLOGY STUDY.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: As soon as practicable after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall enter into a contract with the National Academy of Sciences and the National Research Council to carry out a study of fuel cell technologies that provides a budget roadmap for the development of fuel cell technologies and the transition from petroleum to hydrogen in a significant percentage of the vehicles sold by 2020.

subsection.heading: Requirements.—
subsection.chapeau: In carrying out the study, the National Academy of Sciences and the National Research Council shall—

paragraph.content: establish as a goal the maximum percentage practicable of vehicles that the National Academy of Sciences and the National Research Council determines can be fueled by hydrogen by 2020;
determine the amount of Federal and private funding required to meet the goal established under paragraph (1);
determine what actions are required to meet the goal established under paragraph (1);

examine the need for expanded and enhanced Federal research and development programs, changes in regulations, grant programs, partnerships between the Federal Government and industry, private sector investments, infrastructure investments by the Federal Government and industry, educational and public information initiatives, and Federal and State tax incentives to meet the goal established under paragraph (1);
consider whether other technologies would be less expensive or could be more quickly implemented than fuel cell technologies to achieve significant reductions in carbon dioxide emissions;

paragraph.chapeau: take into account any reports relating to fuel cell technologies and hydrogen-fueled vehicles, including—

subparagraph.content: the report prepared by the National Academy of Engineering and the National Research Council in 2004 entitled “Hydrogen Economy: Opportunities, Costs, Barriers, and R&D Needs”; and
the report prepared by the U.S. Fuel Cell Council in 2003 entitled “Fuel Cells and Hydrogen: The Path Forward”;

paragraph.content: consider the challenges, difficulties, and potential barriers to meeting the goal established under paragraph (1); and

paragraph.chapeau: with respect to the budget roadmap—

subparagraph.content: specify the amount of funding required on an annual basis from the Federal Government and industry to carry out the budget roadmap; and
specify the advantages and disadvantages to moving toward the transition to hydrogen in vehicles in accordance with the timeline established by the budget roadmap.

subsection.heading: Definition of Passive Solar Technology.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section, the term “passive solar technology” means a passive solar technology, including daylighting, that—

paragraph.content: is used exclusively to avoid electricity use; and
can be metered to determine energy savings.

subsection.heading: Study.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall conduct a study to determine—

paragraph.content: the range of levelized costs of avoided electricity for passive solar technologies;
the quantity of electricity displaced using passive solar technologies in the United States as of the date of enactment of this Act; and

paragraph.chapeau: the projected energy savings from passive solar technologies in 5, 10, 15, 20, and 25 years after the date of enactment of this Act if—

subparagraph.content: incentives comparable to the incentives provided for electricity generation technologies were provided for passive solar technologies; and
no new incentives for passive solar technologies were provided.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.content: Not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report that describes the results of the study under subsection (b).

section.heading: STUDY OF LINK BETWEEN ENERGY SECURITY AND INCREASES IN VEHICLE MILES TRAVELED.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall enter into an arrangement with the National Academy of Sciences under which the Academy shall conduct a study to assess the implications on energy use and efficiency of land development patterns in the United States.

subsection.heading: Scope.—
subsection.chapeau: The study shall consider—

paragraph.content: the correlation, if any, between land development patterns and increases in vehicle miles traveled;
whether petroleum use in the transportation sector can be reduced through changes in the design of development patterns;

paragraph.chapeau: the potential benefits of—

subparagraph.content: information and education programs for State and local officials (including planning officials) on the potential for energy savings through planning, design, development, and infrastructure decisions;
incorporation of location efficiency models in transportation infrastructure planning and investments; and

transportation policies and strategies to help transportation planners manage the demand for the number and length of vehicle trips, including trips that increase the viability of other means of travel; and

paragraph.content: such other considerations relating to the study topic as the National Academy of Sciences finds appropriate.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.content: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the National Academy of Sciences shall submit to the Secretary and Congress a report on the study conducted under this section.

section.heading: SCIENCE STUDY ON CUMULATIVE IMPACTS OF MULTIPLE OFFSHORE LIQUEFIED NATURAL GAS FACILITIES.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary (in consultation with the National Oceanic Atmospheric Administration, the Commandant of the Coast Guard, affected recreational and commercial fishing industries, and affected energy and transportation stakeholders) shall carry out a study and compile existing science (including studies and data) to determine the risks or benefits presented by cumulative impacts of multiple offshore liquefied natural gas facilities reasonably assumed to be constructed in an area of the Gulf of Mexico using the open-rack vaporization system.

subsection.heading: Accuracy.—
subsection.content: In carrying out subsection (a), the Secretary shall verify the accuracy of available science and develop a science-based evaluation of significant short-term and long-term cumulative impacts, both adverse and beneficial, of multiple offshore liquefied natural gas facilities reasonably assumed to be constructed in an area of the Gulf of Mexico using or proposing the open-rack vaporization system on the fisheries and marine populations in the vicinity of the facility.

section.heading: ENERGY AND WATER SAVING MEASURES IN CONGRESSIONAL BUILDINGS.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: The Architect of the Capitol, as part of the process of updating the Master Plan Study for the Capitol complex, shall—

paragraph.chapeau: carry out a study to evaluate the energy infrastructure of the Capitol complex to determine how to augment the infrastructure to become more energy efficient—

subparagraph.content: by using unconventional and renewable energy resources;

subparagraph.chapeau: by—

clause.content: incorporating new technologies to implement effective green building solutions;
adopting computer-based building management systems; and
recommending strategies based on end-user behavioral changes to implement low-cost environmental gains; and

subparagraph.content: in a manner that would enable the Capitol complex to have reliable utility service in the event of power fluctuations, shortages, or outages;

paragraph.chapeau: carry out a study to explore the feasibility of installing energy and water conservation measures on the rooftop of the Dirksen Senate Office Building, including the area directly above the food service facilities in the center of the building, including the installation of—

subparagraph.chapeau: a vegetative covering area, using native species to the maximum extent practicable, to—

clause.content: insulate and increase the energy efficiency of the building;
reduce precipitation runoff and conserve water for landscaping or other uses;
increase, and provide more efficient use of, available outdoor space through management of the rooftop of the center of the building as a park or garden area for occupants of the building; and
improve the aesthetics of the building; and

subparagraph.chapeau: onsite renewable energy and other state-of-the-art technologies to—

clause.content: improve the energy efficiency and energy security of the building or the Capitol complex by providing additional or backup sources of power in the event of a power shortage or other emergency;
reduce the use of resources by the building; or
enhance worker productivity; and

subparagraph.content: not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, submit to Congress a report describing the findings and recommendations of the study under subparagraph (B).

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Architect of the Capitol to carry out this section $2,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2006 through 2010.

section.heading: STUDY OF AVAILABILITY OF SKILLED WORKERS.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall enter into an arrangement with the National Academy of Sciences under which the National Academy of Sciences shall conduct a study of the short-term and long-term availability of skilled workers to meet the energy and mineral security requirements of the United States.

subsection.heading: Inclusions.—
subsection.chapeau: The study shall include an analysis of—

paragraph.content: the need for and availability of workers for the oil, gas, and mineral industries;
the availability of skilled labor at both entry level and more senior levels; and
recommendations for future actions needed to meet future labor requirements.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.content: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report that describes the results of the study.

section.heading: REVIEW OF ENERGY POLICY ACT OF 1992 PROGRAMS.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this section, the Secretary shall complete a study to determine the effect that titles III, IV, and V of the Energy Policy Act of 1992 (42 U.S.C. 13211 et seq.) have had on—

paragraph.content: the development of alternative fueled vehicle technology;
the availability of that technology in the market; and
the cost of alternative fueled vehicles.

subsection.heading: Topics.—
subsection.chapeau: As part of the study under subsection (a), the Secretary shall specifically identify—

paragraph.content: the number of alternative fueled vehicles acquired by fleets or covered persons required to acquire alternative fueled vehicles;
the quantity, by type, of alternative fuel actually used in alternative fueled vehicles acquired by fleets or covered persons;
the quantity of petroleum displaced by the use of alternative fuels in alternative fueled vehicles acquired by fleets or covered persons;

paragraph.chapeau: the direct and indirect costs of compliance with requirements under titles III, IV, and V of the Energy Policy Act of 1992 (42 U.S.C. 13211 et seq.), including—

subparagraph.content: vehicle acquisition requirements imposed on fleets or covered persons;
administrative and recordkeeping expenses;
fuel and fuel infrastructure costs;
associated training and employee expenses; and

any other factors or expenses the Secretary determines to be necessary to compile reliable estimates of the overall costs and benefits of complying with programs under those titles for fleets, covered persons, and the national economy;

paragraph.content: the existence of obstacles preventing compliance with vehicle acquisition requirements and increased use of alternative fuel in alternative fueled vehicles acquired by fleets or covered persons; and
the projected impact of amendments to the Energy Policy Act of 1992 made by this title.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.content: Upon completion of the study under this section, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report that describes the results of the study and includes any recommendations of the Secretary for legislative or administrative changes concerning the alternative fueled vehicle requirements under titles III, IV and V of the Energy Policy Act of 1992 (42 U.S.C. 13211 et seq.).

section.heading: STUDY ON THE BENEFITS OF ECONOMIC DISPATCH.

subsection.heading: Study.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary, in coordination and consultation with the States, shall conduct a study on—

paragraph.content: the procedures currently used by electric utilities to perform economic dispatch;
identifying possible revisions to those procedures to improve the ability of nonutility generation resources to offer their output for sale for the purpose of inclusion in economic dispatch; and

the potential benefits to residential, commercial, and industrial electricity consumers nationally and in each state if economic dispatch procedures were revised to improve the ability of nonutility generation resources to offer their output for inclusion in economic dispatch.

subsection.heading: Definition.—
subsection.content: The term “economic dispatch” when used in this section means the operation of generation facilities to produce energy at the lowest cost to reliably serve consumers, recognizing any operational limits of generation and transmission facilities.

subsection.heading: Report to Congress and the States.—
subsection.content: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, and on a yearly basis following, the Secretary shall submit a report to Congress and the States on the results of the study conducted under subsection (a), including recommendations to Congress and the States for any suggested legislative or regulatory changes.

subsection.heading: National Academy of Sciences Study.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the Interior shall enter into a contract with the National Academy of Sciences under which the National Academy of Sciences shall—

paragraph.content: study the potential of developing wind, solar, and ocean energy resources (including tidal, wave, and thermal energy) on Federal land available for those uses under current law and the outer Continental Shelf;
assess any Federal law (including regulations) relating to the development of those resources that is in existence on the date of enactment of this Act; and
recommend statutory and regulatory mechanisms for developing those resources.

subsection.heading: Submission to Congress.—
subsection.content: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the Interior shall submit to Congress the results of the study under subsection (a).

section.heading: INCREASED HYDROELECTRIC GENERATION AT EXISTING FEDERAL FACILITIES.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary, and the Secretary of the Army shall jointly conduct a study of the potential for increasing electric power production capability at federally owned or operated water regulation, storage, and conveyance facilities.

subsection.heading: Content.—
subsection.content: The study under this section shall include identification and description in detail of each facility that is capable, with or without modification, of producing additional hydroelectric power, including estimation of the existing potential for the facility to generate hydroelectric power.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretaries shall submit to the Committees on Energy and Commerce, Resources, and Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate a report on the findings, conclusions, and recommendations of the study under this section by not later than 18 months after the date of the enactment of this Act. The report shall include each of the following:

paragraph.content: The identifications, descriptions, and estimations referred to in subsection (b).
A description of activities currently conducted or considered, or that could be considered, to produce additional hydroelectric power from each identified facility.
A summary of prior actions taken by the Secretaries to produce additional hydroelectric power from each identified facility.

The costs to install, upgrade, or modify equipment or take other actions to produce additional hydroelectric power from each identified facility and the level of Federal power customer involvement in the determination of such costs.

The benefits that would be achieved by such installation, upgrade, modification, or other action, including quantified estimates of any additional energy or capacity from each facility identified under subsection (b).

A description of actions that are planned, underway, or might reasonably be considered to increase hydroelectric power production by replacing turbine runners, by performing generator upgrades or rewinds, or construction of pumped storage facilities.
The impact of increased hydroelectric power production on irrigation, water supply, fish, wildlife, Indian tribes, river health, water quality, navigation, recreation, fishing, and flood control.

Any additional recommendations to increase hydroelectric power production from, and reduce costs and improve efficiency at, federally owned or operated water regulation, storage, and conveyance facilities.

section.heading: SPLIT-ESTATE FEDERAL OIL AND GAS LEASING AND DEVELOPMENT PRACTICES.

subsection.heading: Review.—
subsection.chapeau: In consultation with affected private surface owners, oil and gas industry, and other interested parties, the Secretary of the Interior shall undertake a review of the current policies and practices with respect to management of Federal subsurface oil and gas development activities and their effects on the privately owned surface. This review shall include—

paragraph.content: a comparison of the rights and responsibilities under existing mineral and land law for the owner of a Federal mineral lease, the private surface owners and the Department;

a comparison of the surface owner consent provisions in section 714 of the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 (30 U.S.C. 1304) concerning surface mining of Federal coal deposits and the surface owner consent provisions for oil and gas development, including coalbed methane production; and

recommendations for administrative or legislative action necessary to facilitate reasonable access for Federal oil and gas activities while addressing surface owner concerns and minimizing impacts to private surface.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of the Interior shall report the results of such review to Congress not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act.

section.heading: RESOLUTION OF FEDERAL RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT CONFLICTS IN THE POWDER RIVER BASIN.

subsection.heading: Review.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary of the Interior shall review Federal and State laws in existence on the date of enactment of this Act in order to resolve any conflict relating to the Powder River Basin in Wyoming and Montana between—

paragraph.content: the development of Federal coal; and
the development of Federal and non-Federal coalbed methane.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.chapeau: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the Interior shall submit to Congress a report that—

paragraph.content: describes methods of resolving a conflict described in subsection (a); and
identifies a method preferred by the Secretary of the Interior, including proposed legislative language, if any, required to implement the method.

section.heading: NATIONAL SECURITY REVIEW OF INTERNATIONAL ENERGY REQUIREMENTS.

subsection.heading: Study.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense and Secretary of Homeland Security, shall conduct a study of the growing energy requirements of the People's Republic of China and the implications of such growth on the political, strategic, economic, or national security interests of the United States, including—

paragraph.content: an assessment of the type, nationality, and location of energy assets that have been sought for investment by entities located in the People's Republic of China;

an assessment of the extent to which investment in energy assets by entities located in the People's Republic of China has been on market-based terms and free from subsidies from the People's Republic of China;

an assessment of the effect of investment in energy assets by entities located in the People's Republic of China on the control by the United States of dual-use and export-controlled technologies, including the effect on current and future access to foreign and domestic sources of rare earth elements used to produce such technologies;
an assessment of the relationship between the Government of the People's Republic of China and energy-related businesses located in the People's Republic of China;

an assessment of the impact on the world energy market of the common practice of entities located in the People's Republic of China of removing the energy assets owned or controlled by such entities from the competitive market, with emphasis on the effect if such practice expands along with the growth in energy consumption of the People's Republic of China;
an examination of the United States energy policy and foreign policy as it relates to ensuring a competitive global energy market;
an examination of the relationship between the United States and the People's Republic of China as it relates to pursuing energy interests in a manner that avoids conflicts; and

a comparison of the appropriate laws and regulations of other nations to determine whether a United States company would be permitted to purchase, acquire, merge, or otherwise establish a joint relationship with an entity whose primary place of business is in that other nation, including the laws and regulations of the People's Republic of China.

subsection.heading: Report and Recommendations.—
subsection.content: Not later than 120 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, shall report to the President and the Congress on the findings of the study described in subsection (a) and any recommendations the Secretaries consider appropriate.

subsection.heading: Regulatory Effect.—
subsection.content: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, any instrumentality of the United States vested with authority to review a transaction that includes an investment in a United States domestic corporation may not conclude a national security review related to an investment in the energy assets of a United States domestic corporation by an entity owned or controlled by the government of the People's Republic of China for 21 days after the report to the President and the Congress, and until the President certifies that he has received the report described in subsection (b).

section.heading: USED OIL RE-REFINING STUDY.
section.content: The Secretary, in consultation with the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, shall undertake a study of the energy and environmental benefits of the re-refining of used lubricating oil and report to Congress within 90 days after enactment of this Act including recommendations of specific steps that can be taken to improve collections of used lubricating oil and increase re-refining and other beneficial re-use of such oil.

section.heading: TRANSMISSION SYSTEM MONITORING.
section.content: Within 6 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission shall study and report to Congress on the steps which must be taken to establish a system to make available to all transmission system owners and Regional Transmission Organizations (as defined in the Federal Power Act) within the Eastern and Western Interconnections real-time information on the functional status of all transmission lines within such Interconnections. In such study, the Commission shall assess technical means for implementing such transmission information system and identify the steps the Commission or Congress must take to require the implementation of such system.

section.heading: REPORT IDENTIFYING AND DESCRIBING THE STATUS OF POTENTIAL HYDROPOWER FACILITIES.

subsection.heading: Report Requirement.—
subsection.content: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Bureau of Reclamation, shall submit to the Committee on Resources of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate a report identifying and describing the status of potential hydropower facilities included in water surface storage studies undertaken by the Secretary for projects that have not been completed or authorized for construction.

subsection.heading: Report Contents.—
subsection.chapeau: The report shall include the following:

paragraph.content: Identification of all surface storage studies authorized by Congress since the enactment of the Reclamation Project Act of 1939 (43 U.S.C. 485 et seq.).
The purposes of each project included within each study identified under paragraph (1).

paragraph.chapeau: The status of each study identified under paragraph (1), including for each study—

subparagraph.content: whether the study is completed or, if not completed, still authorized;
the level of analyses conducted at the feasibility and reconnaissance levels of review;
identifiable environmental impacts of each project included in the study, including to fish and wildlife, water quality, and recreation;
projected water yield from each such project;
beneficiaries of each such project;
the amount authorized and expended;
projected funding needs and timelines for completing the study (if applicable);
anticipated costs of each such project; and
other factors that might interfere with construction of any such project.

paragraph.content: An identification of potential hydroelectric facilities that might be developed pursuant to each study identified under paragraph (1).
Applicable costs and benefits associated with potential hydroelectric production pursuant to each study.
